tasks.verified: Requires the restored five-token day_part guidance (including outside and the after-X family) in every extraction node of the generated graph, the gate extended to fail any graph whose day_part omits the outside token, a tenth red-proof mutation proving that extension, the gate still failing v56, and the graph delta confined to extraction descriptions versus v59.
tasks.spec:
You are repairing a regression that a diagnostic run just exposed, in an SMS booking pathway under supervisory rulings. BOUNDARY: write only inside your task directory; never call an API, never mint, never git commit. You own exactly five output files: build_v60.py, v60_graph.json, check_candidate_gate.py, redproof_run.py, report.md. Copy build_v59.py, check_candidate_gate.py and redproof_run.py from ./source/ and edit the copies; run build_v60.py to produce v60_graph.json (adjust its output filename constant).

THE REGRESSION, read ./source/DIAGNOSTIC-FAILURES.txt first. Version 57 classified day_part into FIVE tokens: morning, afternoon, late, outside, none — where outside covered exact clock times outside clinic hours (3am, 11pm) and routed to an honest miss node. A later rewrite of that guidance reduced it to four tokens with a clock-time band mapping, silently deleting outside and dropping the 'after X' phrasing family. Live consequences on the diagnostic run: a 3am request was routed to a late-afternoon OFFER instead of the honest miss; a follow-up then treated an offer as pending booking context; and 'after 3pm works for me' extracted as afternoon, offering 1:00 pm — violating the requested floor. The routing (day_part == outside -> n_miss_time on n_search) is intact in the graph; only the extraction guidance can no longer emit the token.

CHANGE 1, build_v60.py: repair the day_part description on EVERY node that carries it. Merge the two generations correctly — the result must contain ALL of: (a) five tokens exactly: morning, afternoon, late, outside, none; (b) v57's outside rule verbatim in spirit: an exact clock time outside normal clinic hours, such as 3am or 11pm, maps to outside (read ./source/v57_graph.json's n_ask day_part description for the original wording); (c) the after-X family restored: after 3, after 4, 3pm or later, late afternoon, the latest, end of day all map to late, with the 3pm boundary stated as exact; (d) noon to 2:59pm maps to afternoon, morning clock times within opening hours map to morning; (e) the existing sentences that day_part is a routing token never sent to the scheduler, never a date or weekday, never blank. Touch NOTHING else in the builder: the vague-week pair mapping, qualifier preservation, and all prompts and routing stay byte-identical. The grading check diffs your graph against v59 and fails you if anything but extraction descriptions moved.

CHANGE 2, check_candidate_gate.py: extend invariant 3 so the gate FAILS any graph whose day_part extraction description lacks the outside token or the after-3pm-to-late mapping — this is the exact blind spot that let the regression through: the gate verified the route exists but never that extraction can emit its token. Word-presence is acceptable here because the alternative was nothing. Keep all other invariants untouched; the gate must still fail source/v56_graph.json.

CHANGE 3, redproof_run.py: add a TENTH mutation that deletes the outside token from a day_part description and prove the extended gate catches it. Printed line becomes mutations_caught=10, and the mutation's registered name must mention outside or day_part.

OUTPUT CONTRACT for report.md: '# v60 day_part Repair' then '## Summary' (max 3 bullets), '## The Merged Guidance' quoting the final day_part description once in full, '## Gate Extension' naming the new invariant check, '## Assumptions'. Under 500 words.
